title: fix(adr-0087): refuse not-required (no-migration-prescription) on a declared Metadata-protocol: narrowed
body:
Fixes #32601

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么:** `check-adr-0087-registration` 门禁现在拒绝在声明 `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` 的 changeset 上使用 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`;`registered` 与有事实核验的类别(`already-registered`、`unpublished`、`runtime-interface-only`、`type-surface-only`、`runtime-export-retired`)照常放行。
- **为什么改:** 收窄就是作者原来能写的东西现在被拒,升级指南和 `os migrate meta` 必须有对应条目;过去只要把修法写成散文、不写箭头或表格,就能绕过这条豁免。存量 63 个 narrowed changeset 里有 40 个就这样没有登记。
- **风险与回滚:** 只判本 PR 新增或新变为 breaking 的 changeset,存量一个都不会变红。在途的 PR #32611 自带的 changeset 正是这种形态,若它晚于本 PR 合并,会被拦下,需要补一个 semantic 条目。回滚就是 revert 本提交。
- **先看:** `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` 里 `scan()` 新加的拒绝分支(紧跟未知类别检查之后,排在 40 字说明检查之前);同文件的 NP 自测电池;`classifyStockChangeset` 的一处对齐。
- **两分钟验证:** `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --self-test`,预期末行 `✓ check-adr-0087-registration --self-test: 739 assertions ...`。
- **需要你做的:** 无,席位落地。

## What changes

Implements the seat decision on the card (option A): when a changeset declares `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (signal (5)), the disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is refused.

- `scan()` refuses that one category on a changeset whose `breakingDeclaration().signals` carry `NARROWED_SIGNAL`. The kind is read through the imported `readMetadataProtocolLine` (inside `breakingDeclaration`), never by a second parser. The refusal runs right after the closed-vocabulary check and before the 40-character justification check, so neither wording nor a justification can earn the category on a narrowing.
- The refusal names the fix: register an entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` (precedent `18.picklist-binding-unknown-refused.ts`) and mark the changeset `adr-0087: registered ENTRY-ID`, or use a category that rests on a checked fact if one is true. It also says that a change that refuses nothing should correct its `Metadata-protocol:` line instead.
- Unchanged: `registered` and every fact-checked category stay open on a narrowing; `added`, `semantic` and `none` keep the catch-all; a malformed or near-miss kind line triggers nothing; stock that was already breaking at the branch point is inherited and never re-judged.
- `NARROWED_SIGNAL` (`'metadata-protocol-narrowed'`) is now one exported constant read by both `breakingDeclaration` and the new refusal.
- `classifyStockChangeset` (`--audit-stock`) no longer labels an unanswered narrowing as `exempt-no-prescription`. It reports it as residue, with the declaration line as evidence, so the audit agrees with the gate.
- Header: a new section, "A declared narrowing owes the upgrade guide", plus a pointer from the `no-migration-prescription` bullet.

## Tests

New self-test battery `NP (#32601)`, with a floor of 29 cases:

- NP-0: the bare fixture is breaking by signal (5) and by nothing else (minor bump, no banner, no `!`, an arm-less `Clause-②:` line).
- NP-R1 / R2: `narrowed` + catch-all is refused, both with signal (5) alone and with the `(narrowing)` arm and a banner. The refusal names the changeset and the semantic-entries directory.
- NP-R3: a too-short justification gets the narrowing refusal, not the length refusal (ordering pin).
- NP-G1: the same body with `registered` (an entry this diff adds) passes.
- NP-G2: `already-registered` stays open on a narrowing.
- NP-G3: `added` / `semantic` / `none` + catch-all pass, and each is asserted to have been JUDGED under the catch-all, not skipped as non-breaking.
- NP-G4: a malformed kind line (`narrowed|added`) refuses nothing and is still judged.
- NP-G5: an inherited `narrowed` + catch-all stock changeset, edited at head, is skipped.
- NP-S1 / S2: the stock classifier reports an unanswered narrowing as residue and an unanswered `semantic` as exempt.

## Acceptance notes

- **Measured on stock** (`8bfbc4ed`, using the gate's own exported `parseChangeset` / `breakingDeclaration` / `readDisposition` over 1101 pending changesets): 243 declare breaking, 63 declare `narrowed`. Of those 63, 40 hold `no-migration-prescription`, 20 are `registered`, 3 are `already-registered`, and 0 carry no marker. The card measured 39 of 62; one more such changeset landed since.
- **Newly failing on this PR's diff:** 0. `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` prints "this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset". Stock is never re-judged (pinned by NP-G5).
- **Open lane PRs** (checked only the three named in the dispatch): PR #32611's added changeset `.changeset/32503-object-grid-column-summary-refused.md` declares `narrowed` and holds `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, so it is a hit. To check it end to end, I put that file on a throwaway commit object over this head and judged it through the CLI. The base script (`8bfbc4ed`) exits 0 (green). This branch exits 1 with the new refusal. Whichever of the two PRs lands second will see it, so I am reporting it here and have not edited that PR. PR #32597 moves `31224` / `32289` to `registered` and is unaffected. PR #32625's changeset is not breaking.
- **The ruling's list of open categories** names four fact-checked categories and leaves out `runtime-export-retired`, which is also fact-checked (`verifyRuntimeExportRetired`). The ruling refuses exactly one category, so `runtime-export-retired` stays open, and the refusal text lists it among the alternatives.
- **ADR-0087** is not edited. The category vocabulary does not change, so the ADR/CATEGORIES set check (`assertInputs`) is unaffected. The ADR's prose about `no-migration-prescription` does not mention the narrowing refusal yet. That is a governed-surface follow-up for the seat, not part of this diff.
- **No ablation.** The dispatch suggested one, but the standing dev contract says scripts are not ablated. Instead, the before/after reading on PR #32611's real changeset (base green, head red) shows the new branch is what refuses it.
- **No changeset.** `scripts/` ships in no package's `files[]` and the root package is private, so this PR carries `skip-changeset`.
